messages.subject: dht function - mrds
parts:
Hello, 

Something came to mind when I read this:  Spatially explicit models for distance sampling data

To estimate abundance, the dht function is used for conventional distance sampling but also for mark-recapture distance sampling.

To account for perception bias in the abundance estimation, we need to divide the abundance by g(0).

As with the mrds model which uses the same function, I wonder if the abundance is already corrected with the mrds model or if we still need to correct the abundance with the perception bias (by dividing with g(0))?

Thank you for your help
Best regards

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] dht function - mrds
parts:
Camille

Several years ago I prepared a document showing the intermediate calculations associated with an MRDS analysis with independent observers and point independence.  That helped me understand how estimates were being created.

The description uses the "elk faecal pellet" data set published by Burt et al. (2014).  One document (MRDS pellet output) shows the output from the R package (which is the same as the output from DistWin). The second document (trail-of-p.pdf) follows the calculations to produce an estimate of the number of pellet groups in the covered region—adjusting for imperfect detectability on the track line. You will see in step 5 of that document how "usual" detection probability is adjusted for imperfect detectability. The resulting product is the value used to adjust number of groups detected into number of groups in the covered area.  The estimated number of groups (2066) is virtually the same as the estimate produced as the very last reported value (2081) in the "MRDS pellet output.pdf" file.
